clinicalScenario: Scope revision for the India draft: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) reperfusion selection and transfer. Fibrinolysis is not the default for every acute coronary syndrome. This targeted revision does not yet supply a complete medication order set.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm the reperfusion diagnosis and call the receiving centre
actions: Obtain and interpret a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) within 10 minutes. A clear STEMI reperfusion decision must not wait for troponin results (MoHFW cardiovascular STG section 2.0; ACC/AHA 2025 section 3.1).
Record symptom onset, first medical contact (FMC), haemodynamics, contraindications and the realistic FMC-to-device time; activate the regional receiving centre.

clinicalManagement.title: Select one reperfusion pathway
actions: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is preferred when timely. A pharmaco-invasive pathway is conditional on symptom timing, expected PCI delay, bleeding safety and an agreed receiving centre; it is never a universal clot-busting-first instruction.
For symptoms <12 hours, use primary PCI with a goal FMC-to-device ≤90 minutes at a PCI-capable centre or ≤120 minutes when hospital transfer is needed (ACC/AHA 2025 section 5.2.1).

branches.condition: No timely primary PCI; fibrinolysis eligible
actions: For symptoms <12 hours and expected FMC-to-device delay >120 minutes, fibrinolysis may be selected only after checking the full contraindication list and agreeing transfer to a PCI-capable hospital. Use an approved weight/age-adjusted drug protocol; this scope revision does not supply an unverified thrombolytic dose (ACC/AHA 2025 section 5.3).

Urgently transfer for PCI when fibrinolysis is contraindicated. Do not give fibrinolysis for non-ST-elevation syndromes; suspected aortic dissection, active bleeding and relevant intracranial history require an explicit safety assessment (ACC/AHA 2025 section 5.3; ESC 2023 Table S11).

branches.condition: Shock, ongoing ischaemia or dangerous arrhythmia
actions: Seek emergency revascularisation and critical-care transfer. Late presentation does not remove the need for urgent assessment when instability or continuing ischaemia is present (ACC/AHA 2025 section 5.2.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Transfer after fibrinolysis and assess reperfusion
actions: Transfer to a PCI-capable hospital after fibrinolysis; treatment at the spoke is not the end of care. Failed reperfusion, persistent pain or haemodynamic/electrical instability requires rescue PCI rather than waiting for routine angiography (MoHFW STG section 3.4; ACC/AHA 2025 section 5.3).
After successful fibrinolysis, plan early angiography/PCI within 2–24 hours under the receiving team (ACC/AHA 2025 section 5.3).
Handover the original/repeat ECGs, all treatment and times, bleeding assessment, renal function and accepting clinician. Use a monitored ambulance with resuscitation capability.

keyPoints: Timely PCI is preferred; fibrinolysis is conditional.
pitfalls: Treating all acute coronary syndromes with thrombolysis.
